question: Which structural layer in some cell types is composed mainly of carbohydrates like cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin in the ratio 4∶ 3∶ 3 and some fatty substances like wax?
solution:
The correct answer is __**cell wall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell walls**

 
 
• Cell walls are **found exclusively in plant cells**, providing them with structural support and protection.
 
• Cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin are the main components of plant cell walls, providing them strength and flexibility.
 
• The** ratio of 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 3 of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin** reflects the chemical composition of the cell wall.
 
• Fatty substances such as **waxes are used to provide water repellent properties** to the cell wall.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 **Details**
 
 

 cell soluble
 Cytoplasm or vacuole is a water-filled sac inside the cell, in which various substances are stored.
 
 

 plasma membrane
 Plasma membrane is the outer layer of the cell which acts as a barrier between the cell and its external environment.
 
 

 nuclear envelope
 The nuclear envelope is a double layer that surrounds the nucleus, which acts as a barrier between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
